messages:
maya: Heads-up — brought up cetus-13b (int4) in staging yesterday. At ~40–60% qps we started seeing intermittent OOMs and sustained heap fragmentation signals from the runtime. Looks correlated with bursts of long responses (max_new_tokens high).
rahul: Any jemalloc/tcmalloc stats? fragmentation + OOM usually points to arena growth or lots of short-lived allocations from batching.
tara: Saw the same on a run — long chat turns (600+ new tokens) were the common factor. Short requests are fine.
maya: Minimal log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-18T14:12:03Z] serve: alloc failed: wanted=1.2GB, avail=900MB
[2026-03-18T14:12:03Z] kv-cache: entries=432, total_tokens=11234
[2026-03-18T14:12:03Z] memfrag: high-water=1.8GB, rss=2.1GB
```
oliver: Two-prong idea: 1) lower default max_new_tokens for cetus canary to limit KV blowup; 2) enable a lightweight "kv priming/warmup" so repeated short turns reuse the same prefetched KV, reducing churn.
rahul: Agreed. Also experiment with allocator tuning: enable background decay and cap arenas per worker. On linux we use MALLOC_CONF for jemalloc; example: `MALLOC_CONF=background_thread:true,decay_time:1s,arena:4` — that reduced fragmentation on phoenix runs.
tara: Proposed quick canary config (staging only):
```
model: cetus-13b-int4
defaults:
  max_new_tokens: 256    # down from 512
  batching:
    max_batch_size: 24
    batch_multiplier: 3
  kv_priming:
    enabled: true
    warmup_prefixes: 2
    reuse_window_s: 15
```
maya: Also want a runtime KV-trim policy to evict older prefixes aggressively when memory high. Draft:
```
runtime:
  kv_trim:
    strategy: lru-by-age
    threshold_mb: 1200
    prune_step_tokens: 128
```
oliver: I can push both changes to the staging canary. Plan: 1) apply allocator env + kv_trim; 2) push model defaults above; 3) run 2h soak at current qps; 4) if no OOMs and latency stable, expand to 10% traffic.
maya: +1. We'll capture memfrag histograms and jemalloc stats every 30s.
ci-bot: deploy-bot: starting canary deployment cetus-13b-int4 -> staging (sha=abc123, group=canary, duration=2h)
rahul: Follow-ups: oliver — add jemalloc stats to /metrics (arena_count, decay_time, retained) and tag traces with "kv_priming=true/false" so we can A/B.
oliver: Will do. Also adding a temporary automatic rollback if OOM rate > 0.1% for 5m.
tara: If this looks good we should document the tradeoff in the model onboarding checklist: prefer smaller max_new_tokens + kv_priming for int4 quantized variants.
maya: Sounds like a plan. I'll own the post-mortem if anything flares. @oliver please ping when canary is live so QA can run targeted prompts. :thumbsup:
oliver: Pinged in #eng-oncall when live. Will post results in ~2.5h.
ci-bot: deploy-bot: canary complete — monitoring window started. No immediate OOMs in first 15m.
maya: thanks, keeping eyes on it.
